narration: You got a raise and celebrated. But in 2022, inflation hit seven-point-nine percent. If your raise was five percent or less, you actually lost purchasing power.
visual: Worker silhouette with fists raised in celebration, paycheck card showing +4% raise in green, red inflation meter slides in from below revealing 7.9%

narration: In 2022, average raises were five percent. Inflation hit seven-point-nine. That gap drained twenty-seven hundred dollars from a seventy-grand salary — and most people never knew.
visual: Two bars growing side by side — green WAGES bar at 5%, taller red INFLATION bar at 7.9%, '$2,700 LOST' badge springs onto screen

narration: Every year this keeps happening, the real cost compounds. Your paycheck looks bigger, but your grocery cart, your rent, your gas — they all know the truth.
visual: Paycheck SVG showing $70,000 salary with a red drain overlay washing over it, counter ticking from $0 to -$2,730 labeled 'purchasing power drained'

narration: HR departments set raise budgets using the same CPI data your landlord does. They know the gap. They're counting on you not doing the math.
visual: HR person at desk pointing at monitor showing spreadsheet with 'CPI forecast 7.9%, Raise budget 5.0%, Real cost to worker -2.9%' and 'Won't raise eyebrows'

narration: Run it over ten years and the gap between your nominal wage and real purchasing power reaches eighteen thousand dollars. That's a car. That's a house down payment.
visual: Animated dual-line chart — green nominal salary line rises steeply, red dashed real buying power line barely moves, $18,000 gap badge springs in at end

narration: Next raise negotiation, don't just ask for a raise — ask for inflation plus your productivity gains. That's how you stop losing ground. Follow for more money truth.
visual: Two people at negotiation table, employee has speech bubble 'CPI + 2% minimum', two action cards slide in with steps 1 and 2, FOLLOW FOR MORE CTA
